sections.heading: A multi-part probability and counting problem

questions.q: This question has two parts. A class has 8 boys and 7 girls. A group of 4 students is selected at random to represent the class. (a) Find the total number of ways to select the group of 4 from the 15 students. (b) Find the probability that the group consists of exactly 2 boys and 2 girls.
questions.answer: (a) $\binom{15}{4}=\dfrac{15!}{4!11!}=1365$. (b) Ways to choose 2 boys and 2 girls: $\binom{8}{2}\times\binom{7}{2}=28\times21=588$. Probability: $\dfrac{588}{1365}\approx0.431$, or about $43.1\%$.

questions.q: Find the number of distinct arrangements of the letters in the word "BANANA".
questions.answer: The word has 6 letters with repeats: A appears 3 times, N appears 2 times. Number of distinct arrangements: $\dfrac{6!}{3!2!}=\dfrac{720}{12}=60$.

questions.q: A committee of 3 is selected from 5 men and 4 women. Given that at least one woman is selected, find the probability that exactly 2 women are selected.
questions.answer: Total ways with at least 1 woman: total ways $\binom{9}{3}=84$ minus all-men ways $\binom{5}{3}=10$, giving $84-10=74$. Ways with exactly 2 women: $\binom{4}{2}\times\binom{5}{1}=6\times5=30$. Conditional probability: $\dfrac{30}{74}=\dfrac{15}{37}\approx0.405$.

questions.q: A student scores at the 85th percentile on a standardized test. Explain what this means in terms of the rest of the test-taking population.
questions.answer: Scoring at the 85th percentile means the student performed better than approximately 85% of all test-takers, and approximately 15% of test-takers scored higher than this student.

questions.q: A die is rolled once. Find $P(\text{rolling an even number or a 5})$, explaining why the addition rule simplifies since these events are mutually exclusive.
questions.answer: Even numbers: $2,4,6$ (3 outcomes). Since 5 is odd, it cannot overlap with the even outcomes — the events are mutually exclusive. $P(\text{even or }5)=P(\text{even})+P(5)=\dfrac{3}{6}+\dfrac{1}{6}=\dfrac{4}{6}=\dfrac{2}{3}$.

sections.heading: A multi-part counting and probability problem with restrictions

questions.q: This question has three parts. A password consists of 4 characters chosen from the 10 digits 0-9, and repetition is not allowed. (a) Find the total number of possible passwords. (b) Find the number of passwords where the first character is not 0 (a common restriction to avoid leading zeros). (c) Find the probability that a randomly generated valid password (from part b) starts with an even digit.
questions.answer: (a) $P(10,4)=10\times9\times8\times7=5040$. (b) First character has 9 choices (1-9, excluding 0); remaining 3 characters chosen from the remaining 9 digits without repetition: $9\times9\times8\times7=4536$. (c) Even first digits from 1-9: $2,4,6,8$ (4 choices). Passwords starting with an even digit: $4\times9\times8\times7=2016$. Probability: $\dfrac{2016}{4536}=\dfrac{4}{9}\approx0.444$.
